open_points.subject: refusal reasons
open_points.text: “refuses with one code of the closed set below and a bounded reason naming the first failing check” does not define the exact reason values, although callers are told to read the reason
open_points.question: What stable reason identifier must each operation return for each own-check refusal, separately from optional explanatory text?
options: A closed reason enumeration shared by all operations
A per-operation closed set of check identifiers
Unstructured bounded text chosen by each module
open_points.default_guess: Use stable per-operation check identifiers plus optional bounded explanatory text.

open_points.subject: actor attribution for automatic work
open_points.text: “Every operation that writes a record receives the acting Actor … from its caller” conflicts with admission and activation being kernel actions, while submit_implementation receives the submitting agent and TrialExecution and AdmissionVerdict have no actor field
open_points.question: Which actor is recorded for trial executions, admission verdicts, approval requests and effect attempts produced automatically inside a user request, and where is that actor stored?
options: Record the kernel for every automatic sub-action
Record the request actor for every record produced by the request
Define an actor separately for each record type and add any missing actor fields
open_points.default_guess: Record the request actor only for the requested action and the kernel for automatic admission or activation work, with explicit actor fields where attribution is required.

open_points.subject: store.spool_file attempt identity
open_points.text: “store alone assigns attempt_number, inside the transaction that writes the record” conflicts with store.spool_file requiring “run_id, node, map_index, attempt_number” before record_run_progress or record_read_outcome writes the NodeExecution
open_points.question: How does runs or effects obtain the attempt_number needed to spool a function output or read-operation output before the store transaction assigns that number?
options: Spool files inside the same record_change that assigns the attempt number
Add a store operation that reserves an attempt number
Let callers calculate the next number before calling spool_file
open_points.default_guess: Publish the files and their records inside the same store change that assigns the attempt number.

open_points.subject: trial file outputs
open_points.text: The named change record_trial_execution writes “one TrialExecution M07 and its output StoredValues”, while M07 says a file output has “only its facts … no bytes and never a StoredValue”
open_points.question: Does a trial execution retain file-output bytes as StoredValues, or discard the bytes and retain only digest, size and media type?
options: Discard file-output bytes and record facts only
Persist file-output bytes as StoredValues
Persist them only when the case has expected file outputs
open_points.default_guess: Discard trial file-output bytes and record only their facts; only trial-case fixtures remain stored.

open_points.subject: sandbox output size validation
open_points.text: sandbox.execute_function says outputs are validated with fit_port_value, but fit_port_value requires a size bound and execute_function does not state which persistence-size bound to use; A15 assigns stored-value and spool-size failures to the caller after sandbox success
open_points.question: Which size checks occur inside the sandbox, and which outcome results when a function output exceeds stored_value_bytes_max, spool_file_bytes_max or the remaining spool_run_bytes_max?
options: Sandbox checks only contract schema and aggregate ResourceBounds.output_bytes; callers check persistence ceilings
Sandbox also checks per-output storage ceilings
Pass all applicable storage ceilings and current spool usage into the sandbox
open_points.default_guess: The sandbox checks schema, carriage and aggregate output_bytes only; runs applies storage and spool ceilings afterward with the outcomes specified by A15.

open_points.subject: unrecorded spooled files
open_points.text: “When a request makes several store changes, those made before the failed one stay” and spool_file publishes bytes before the later record_run_progress or record_attempt_outcome change, but startup removes only temporary files and spools of ended runs
open_points.question: What happens to published spool files when the later record change fails or the process stops before their SpooledFile record is written?
options: Remove every file not referenced by a SpooledFile record during recovery
Remove the current attempt's files immediately when the record change fails
Make spool publication and record creation one atomic store operation
open_points.default_guess: Make spool publication and the corresponding record creation atomic; otherwise recovery should remove unreferenced spool files.

open_points.subject: inspection of trial file fixtures
open_points.text: “a file — StoredValue fixture or SpooledFile — [is returned] as digest, size and media type, its bytes only through read_spooled_file”, but read_spooled_file “takes only a SpooledFile — never a StoredValue”
open_points.question: Through which operation can the owner read the bytes of a trial-case file fixture, as required by inspection and the rule that the owner receives every value?
options: Allow read_spooled_file to accept file-carriage StoredValues too
Add a separate owner-only read_trial_fixture operation
Declare that fixture bytes are not inspectable
open_points.default_guess: Add an owner-only operation for reading a file-carriage StoredValue fixture.

open_points.subject: get_repair_view without an activation
open_points.text: get_repair_view requires “the current implementation through functions.read_implementation”, but a slot's current contract version can have no current activation after issuance or refused admission
open_points.question: What does get_repair_view return when the current contract version has no activated implementation?
options: Return current_implementation as absent and still return the contract and corpus
Refuse the repair view
Use the activation of an earlier contract version
open_points.default_guess: Return the current contract and corpus with no current implementation.

open_points.subject: approval preview masking
open_points.text: An approval preview contains “the built request” including URL, headers and body, while an agent must receive personal-data inputs only as digest and class; personal values may already be embedded in the URL, query or JSON body
open_points.question: How is the built-request portion of an approval preview represented and masked for an agent without exposing personal-data input values embedded in it?
options: Store a structured request description whose input-derived fields can be replaced by digest and class
Hide the entire request description from agents when any input is personal_data
Return the description unchanged because the separate input list is masked
open_points.default_guess: Use a structured preview and replace every personal-data-derived component with its digest and class for agents.

open_points.subject: mutable entity records
open_points.text: store.read_records says “records are never edited (A01 rule 6)”, while named changes mutate bindings, runs, approvals, attempts and grants through accepted, approved, used, resolved and revoked statuses
open_points.question: Are lifecycle transitions updates to one stored entity record, or immutable transition records from which the current entity is projected?
options: Update the mutable fields of the entity record in place
Append immutable transition records and derive current state
Use updates for some entity types and transition records for others, explicitly enumerated
open_points.default_guess: Update the mutable entity models in place while keeping the record types explicitly protected by A01 rule 6 immutable.

open_points.subject: store order of mutable records
open_points.text: List operations return records in reverse store order, but the texts do not say whether accepting, approving, resolving or revoking an existing entity changes that entity's store position
open_points.question: For paging and newest-first lists, is a mutable entity ordered by creation, by its latest transition, or by a separate transition record?
options: Keep its original creation position forever
Move it to a new position on every transition
List lifecycle transitions separately from entities
open_points.default_guess: Keep an entity's original creation position; only newly created records receive new positions.

open_points.subject: paging under mutable status filters
open_points.text: A continuation token is “the store position of the last item returned” and must name “a position of that list”, but filters include mutable status fields whose records can enter or leave the filtered list between pages
open_points.question: How does page_records continue when the cursor record or other records change status between page requests?
options: Treat the token as an absolute store-position cursor and evaluate the filter at each page
Bind the token to a snapshot of list membership
Reject the token if the cursor record no longer matches the filter
open_points.default_guess: Use the absolute store position as the cursor and apply the current filter only to records below it.

open_points.subject: service api_base_url
open_points.text: An api_base_url is accepted when it is “an absolute http or https URL with a host”, then the request URL is formed by removing a trailing slash and appending the declared path
open_points.question: Are userinfo, an existing path, query, fragment, IPv6 zone identifier or percent-encoded authority allowed in api_base_url, and exactly how is the Host header authority derived from them?
options: Restrict api_base_url to scheme, host and optional port only
Allow a base path but forbid userinfo, query and fragment
Allow every absolute URL form and define a complete joining and authority algorithm
open_points.default_guess: Restrict api_base_url to scheme, host and optional port, with no userinfo, path, query or fragment.

open_points.subject: plain-http loopback test
open_points.text: Plain HTTP is allowed when the api_base_url “host is a loopback address”, without defining whether this means an IP literal, a hostname such as localhost, or a DNS result
open_points.question: What exact hosts qualify as loopback, and is DNS resolution involved in that decision?
options: Only canonical IPv4 or IPv6 loopback literals
Loopback literals and the hostname localhost
Any hostname whose resolved address is loopback
open_points.default_guess: Accept only IP literals classified as loopback, avoiding a DNS-dependent policy decision.

open_points.subject: service file-output spool failures
open_points.text: send_prepared_request promises “one outcome name of the A09 rule 5 table”, whose 2xx validation includes spool ceilings, while State 3 says service_invoker “judges only the response ceiling and never sees the run's spool” and store.spool_file owns both spool ceilings
open_points.question: What result does send_prepared_request return before spooling, and which module converts a spool ceiling refusal into the final NodeExecution status and EffectAttempt status?
options: Invoker returns a provisional successful response and effects determines the final outcome after spooling
Pass run spool state into the invoker so it returns the final A09 outcome
Make store.spool_file return a fully classified operation outcome
open_points.default_guess: The invoker returns a validated provisional response; effects spools it and records contract_violation with attempt applied if a spool ceiling is exceeded.

open_points.subject: guards on many or mapped outputs
open_points.text: A guard compares a source output value with one member of a closed set, while mapped-node outputs and many ports produce lists; no proof rule forbids a guard port with cardinality many or a guard sourced from a mapped node
open_points.question: Are guards permitted on many-valued or mapped outputs, and if so is the guard evaluated once on the whole list or separately for each element?
options: Require every guard port to have cardinality one and not be a mapped output
Compare the whole collected list with the guard value
Evaluate the guard independently for each mapped element
open_points.default_guess: The proof should require a scalar, non-mapped guard port.

open_points.subject: standing grant observable effect
open_points.text: grant_standing_approval says “Later sends of that node in runs of that version need no approval”, but the same texts say grants for read or draft-write nodes are never used and every resend after not_applied requires a fresh approval
open_points.question: What precise effect should the grant operation promise for each effect class and for a resend after not_applied?
options: Only state-transition and external-effect sends may use the grant, except resends after not_applied
Every non-destructive send may use the grant
Forbid grants on read and draft-write nodes because they have no effect
open_points.default_guess: A grant affects only ordinary state-transition and external-effect sends; it has no effect on read or draft-write sends and never covers a resend after not_applied.

open_points.subject: module read-operation outputs
open_points.text: “Records reach a caller as they are” conflicts with read_contract_version, read_implementation, read_binding and read_flow_version listing only selected fields and omitting other State 1 fields such as identities, creators and timestamps
open_points.question: Do these read operations return the complete corresponding model record, or only the fields explicitly listed in each Outputs section?
options: Return the complete model record plus any named derived data
Return only the explicitly listed projection
Define a distinct response model for every read operation
open_points.default_guess: Return the complete model record, with explicit masking or code omission applied by surface, plus any named derived data.
